Whales are holders of very large amounts of a cryptocurrency. Whales can move token prices significantly when they buy or sell. Whales are often viewed with suspicion in DeFi forums because their trades can be used to manipulate markets.

Pump and dump scam is a coordinated scheme in which promoters inflate the price of a token through hype. Pump and dump scam ends when the promoters sell their holdings at the inflated price. Pump and dump scam leaves late buyers holding tokens that lose most of their value.

AMA is an abbreviation for Ask Me Anything, a question-and-answer session. AMA sessions are typically held in social media or community channels. AMA sessions involve a project team answering questions from community members.

Hacker is a person who exploits vulnerabilities in software, smart contracts or systems. Hacker attacks can lead to the theft of user funds. Hacker activity is a recurring risk warning in DeFi communities.

Greater fool theory is the belief that an asset can be sold at a profit to a buyer who pays more, regardless of its intrinsic value. Greater fool theory explains price rises driven by speculation rather than fundamentals. Greater fool theory describes a market in which losses fall on the last buyers.
